headline_marked: Record chase: [[West Indies beat India by 6 wickets]] to level series
headline: Record chase: West Indies beat India by 6 wickets to level series
summary: Shai Hope's unbeaten 102 and Sherfane Rutherford's 84 power the Windies to a historic 250-run chase in Ranchi.
details: West Indies achieved their highest successful chase in T20 internationals, overhauling a target of 250 to defeat India by six wickets in Ranchi.
Skipper Shai Hope anchored the victory with an unbeaten 102 off 45 balls, while Sherfane Rutherford contributed a blistering 84 off 37 deliveries.
The victory levels the five-match series at 1-1 after a daunting chase that saw the Windies lose early wickets to Mayank Yadav.
Hope and Rutherford turned the match around with a crucial 120-run partnership for the fourth wicket.
This marks the second-highest successful run chase in men's T20 international history, only surpassed by South Africa's pursuit of 259 in 2023.
Earlier, India posted 249-5, driven by Sanju Samson's 82 off 41 balls and a late surge by Shreyas Iyer and Tilak Varma.
Despite India's massive total, West Indies managed to reach the target with nine balls to spare.
caption:
A historic chase! West Indies pull off the second-highest successful run chase in T20I history to stun India.

West Indies achieved their highest successful chase in T20 internationals, overhauling a target of 250 to defeat India by six wickets in Ranchi.

Skipper Shai Hope anchored the victory with an unbeaten 102 off 45 balls, while Sherfane Rutherford contributed a blistering 84 off 37 deliveries.

The victory levels the five-match series at 1-1 after a daunting chase that saw the Windies lose early wickets to Mayank Yadav.

Hope and Rutherford turned the match around with a crucial 120-run partnership for the fourth wicket.

This marks the second-highest successful run chase in men's T20 international history, only surpassed by South Africa's pursuit of 259 in 2023.

Earlier, India posted 249-5, driven by Sanju Samson's 82 off 41 balls and a late surge by Shreyas Iyer and Tilak Varma.

Despite India's massive total, West Indies managed to reach the target with nine balls to spare.

headline_marked: South African jurist [[Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize]]
headline: South African jurist Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize
summary: The lifelong human rights champion and former ICC judge has addressed genocide allegations in Gaza, Rwanda, and Myanmar.
details: South African jurist Navi Pillay, a lifelong human rights champion, has been awarded the Nobel Peace Prize. The prize includes a gold medal, a diploma, and $1.2 million.
Pillay, 85, is currently a judge at the International Court of Justice (ICJ) and has previously served as UN Commissioner for Human Rights and a judge at the International Criminal Court (ICC).
The Norwegian Nobel Committee stated that Pillay's expertise and steadfastness have made her one of the most respected international jurists of our time.
Pillay dedicated her award to the survivors of international crimes and emphasized that world leaders have a legal obligation to protect human rights and refrain from war.
The award has sparked controversy, with Israel reacting angrily, claiming the prize legitimizes 'anti-Israel hatred' and that the committee has 'lost its moral compass'.

Simultaneously, the United States has announced sanctions on the ICC, vowing to cripple its operations. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that Washington would ban transactions with the 'rogue court'.
The ICC rejected the sanctions as an attack on international law, while Canada, France, Germany, Japan, and the UK expressed strong disagreement with the US move.
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called the US sanctions a 'serious blow' to the pursuit of international criminal justice.
caption:
A lifelong champion of human rights and a former ICC judge has just been awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.

South African jurist Navi Pillay, a lifelong human rights champion, has been awarded the Nobel Peace Prize. The prize includes a gold medal, a diploma, and $1.2 million.

Pillay, 85, is currently a judge at the International Court of Justice (ICJ) and has previously served as UN Commissioner for Human Rights and a judge at the International Criminal Court (ICC).

The Norwegian Nobel Committee stated that Pillay's expertise and steadfastness have made her one of the most respected international jurists of our time.

Pillay dedicated her award to the survivors of international crimes and emphasized that world leaders have a legal obligation to protect human rights and refrain from war.

The award has sparked controversy, with Israel reacting angrily, claiming the prize legitimizes 'anti-Israel hatred' and that the committee has 'lost its moral compass'.

Simultaneously, the United States has announced sanctions on the ICC, vowing to cripple its operations. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that Washington would ban transactions with the 'rogue court'.

The ICC rejected the sanctions as an attack on international law, while Canada, France, Germany, Japan, and the UK expressed strong disagreement with the US move.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called the US sanctions a 'serious blow' to the pursuit of international criminal justice.
